speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific characteristics of your wrist pain, including when it started and what makes it better or worse.

Also, can you tell me about the fever and the skin lesions? Are the lesions itchy, painful, or associated with any other symptoms like joint swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis (Left Wrist) secondary to disseminated gonococcal infection.

I suspect a joint infection given the acute onset of pain, fever, and chills, especially with your history of recent sexually active contact and a prior episode of knee pain. Given your camping trip in Minnesota, I also need to consider Lyme disease, though the sexual history points more strongly toward Gonorrhea.

Do you have any other joint pain, a rash elsewhere on your body, or symptoms like tendonitis?
